summary: With the author's sentinel line stripped by fixups.json the original now compiles and renders, and the pair is judgeable for the first time: both sides are the same multi-mode music-sequencer animation and even agree exactly on the sequencer grid pitch (36 cells of ~7.1 px on a 256-px rig), but the port drives its pixels off the x coordinate where the original is index-only (so on the default 16x16 grid the port draws vertical columns while the original draws contiguous index runs), its super-cycle is 36.9 s against the original's 27.0 s, its opening VU bar is ~4x too slow, and several modes are in the wrong hue family.
observations: HARNESS/PROVENANCE: both sides now compile and render. meta.json warnings carry `fixups.json: stripped 1 line(s) from the ORIGINAL matching REMOVE_THIS_INVALID_LINE_IF_YOU_UNDERSTAND_THIS_WARNING`, provenance.fixups.source.removed = 1. epeSha256 8cd5a175956c, portSha256 137ed0551bcd, harnessSha256 bfd91d43d7f9. Default rig is grid 16x16 / 256 px. Both sides: compileError null, runtimeError null, wantsSensors true, sensors "synth", sensorModel "beat120". Both sides expose ZERO settable controls (--probe-controls prints "(no settable controls)" for orig and port alike), so there is no dial surface to compare and no dial mismatch.

PIXEL-ADDRESSING MODE — the single biggest divergence. The ORIGINAL is INDEX-ONLY: its flat pixel sequence is byte-identical (mean abs diff 0.00/px at t=0.65, 1.15 and 3.35 s) across strip-256, grid 16x16 and grid 32x8. The PORT is COORDINATE(x)-DRIVEN: the same three dumps differ by 39.4 / 54.5 / 21.1 abs/px between grid 16x16 and strip, and on grid 32x8 every row is identical (row 0 == row 3 == `144 x6, 0 x26`), i.e. the port's output is constant down each column and carries only gridWidth distinct values per frame. Consequence on the DEFAULT 16x16 rig: at t=0.65 s the original lights flat indices 77..255 at (153,0,0) — which reads as the bottom 11.2 rows of the grid — while the port lights columns 0..2 on every row at (144,0,0), i.e. a vertical bar. Every mode inherits this: the original's contact sheets are horizontal bands and diagonal textures, the port's are vertical stripes throughout.

OPENING MODE (VU/level bar), measured on strip-256 at 20 fps, dumps every 0.05 s: ORIGINAL grows a solid bar at 13 px per 0.05 s = 260 px/s, filling all 256 px in ~0.98 s, then blanks for 1-2 frames and restarts from the OTHER end (right-fill 0.00-0.90 s, left-fill 1.05-1.45 s, right-fill 1.60-2.00 s). PORT grows the same solid bar at 3.3 px per 0.05 s = 66 px/s, taking ~3.9 s to fill (n=4 at t=0, n=254 at t=3.85), then blanks one frame and refills from the far end over the next ~4.2 s. Ratio 3.94x — the port advances 1/8 of the strip per beat where the original advances 1/2 per beat.

BEAT ENVELOPE in that mode: both sides re-trigger on a 0.5 s (2 Hz / 120 BPM) grid, but the decay shape differs. ORIGINAL is a LINEAR ramp to zero: 229, 203, 178, 153, 127, 102, 76, 51, 25, then a fully black frame, every 0.5 s (peak is a constant 229 each beat). PORT decays exponentially to a non-zero floor: 249, 218, 190, 165, 144, 126, 112, 101, 94, 90 — i.e. it bottoms out at ~36% of peak and never goes dark between beats, and its peak drifts down across a bar (249, 244, 239, 233, 228, 223) instead of holding constant.

SUPER-CYCLE PERIOD (autocorrelation of raw meanBrightness, mean-subtracted full lag scan, strip-256): ORIGINAL 275 f @10 fps = 27.5 s (r=0.990), 539 f @20 fps = 26.9 s (r=0.985), 1059 f @40 fps = 26.5 s (r=0.995) — essentially fps-invariant at ~27 s, with clean 2x/3x harmonics. PORT 433 f @10 fps = 43.3 s (r=0.873), 738 f @20 fps = 36.9 s (r=0.725), 1456 f @40 fps = 36.4 s (r=0.843) — 1.37x too long at 20/40 fps and additionally NOT fps-stable (43.3 s at 10 fps vs 36.4-36.9 s at 20/40 fps), so the port's mode advance has a frame-rate-sensitive term the original does not.

MODE INVENTORY over one full cycle each (strip-256, 20 fps, dumps every 0.3 s). ORIGINAL, 27.0 s cycle: (1) 0.0-2.0 s red VU bar alternating ends ~1 s/sweep; (2) 2.1-3.15 s a 60-px internally-graded block ping-ponging the length of the strip, ~1.05 s round trip, peak ~250; (3) 3.2-4.15 s full-strip symmetric TRIANGLE gradient peaking exactly at index 128 (128 distinct values), red with a small blue component (hue 336-355), re-struck each beat; (4) 4.25-5.95 s a 32-px block stepping one 32-px slot per 0.5 s beat (224->192->160->128->96->64->32), hue drifting red -> white; (5) 6.3-8.4 s 30/31-px blocks alternating between the two ENDS with fully saturated primaries per step (green 144deg, magenta 288, yellow 72, blue 216, red 0); (6) 8.7-9.6 s a 48-px block at centre; (7) 9.9-10.8 s black; (8) 11.1-18.6 s the 'fan'; (9) 19.2-26.4 s the sequencer grid; (10) 26.7 s black, restart. PORT, 36.9 s cycle: (1) 0.0-8.1 s the two slow VU sweeps; (2) 8.4-12.0 s a full-strip ORANGE (hue 14) symmetric bloom peaked at 128; (3) 12.3-15.9 s a 32-px stepping block in warm yellow/orange (hue 2-69); (4) 16.2-19.8 s 72-px and 43-px saturated blocks with a green->cyan hue walk; (5) 20.1-20.7 s black; (6) 21.0-28.8 s the 'fan' analogue; (7) 29.1-36.6 s the sequencer grid; restart. The ORDER corresponds, but the port has no analogue of the original's ping-pong block (2), its triangle gradient (3) or its 48-px centre block (6), and it spends ~8 s on the bar mode where the original spends ~2 s.

'FAN' MODE (orig 11.1-18.6 s, port 21.0-28.8 s), profiles dumped every 0.1 s. ORIGINAL is a PERSISTENT, heavily textured standing field: peak brightness never leaves 184-244, the peak pixel stays near index 107-126, and the profile is broken into 4-14 separate lit runs with fine dither, giving the waterfall its speckled chevron/'tree' texture; its hue walks blue 187 -> purple 208 -> magenta 253 -> red/pink 300-320 -> red 241 -> orange 180 -> yellow-green 138 across the mode. PORT is a beat-triggered RIPPLE: a single lit run (runs=1, whole strip lit) that flashes at the centre (peak index exactly 128, v=253) and then decays and spreads outward (v 253 -> 187 -> 122 -> 58 over ~0.9 s, peak index migrating to r=65 from centre) before the next strike; its hue walks yellow-green 84 -> green 133 -> teal 170 -> cyan 194 -> blue 231. So the original's fan is red/magenta/purple/blue and continuously textured; the port's is green/cyan/blue, smooth, and strobed.

SEQUENCER MODE — the geometry MATCHES EXACTLY and is the strongest point in the port's favour. Frame dumps (orig t=22.5 s, port t=32.0 s) show both sides drawing the same cell lattice: separator pixels at flat indices 0, 8, 15, 22, 29, 36, 43, 50, 57, 64, 72, 79, 86, 93, 100, 107, 114, 121, 128, 136, 143, 150, 157, 164, 171, 178, 185, 192, 200, 207, 214, 221, 228, 235, 242, 249 — 36 cells at a ~7.1 px pitch on both sides. Note blocks are one cell wide on both (mean bright-run width orig 7.0 px, port 7.3 px) and drawn from the same saturated-primary family (orig: 255/0/0, 255/102/0, 101/203/0, 0/255/255, 0/57/255, 255/0/224; port: 255/127/0, 127/255/0, 0/255/0, 0/255/255, 0/0/255, 127/0/255, 255/0/127).

SEQUENCER MODE — three measurable divergences. (a) NOTE DENSITY: over the full mode window the ORIGINAL averages 0.22 bright (max channel >=180) runs per frame (46 samples over 19.5-26.25 s) while the PORT averages 2.60 (53 samples over 29.0-36.8 s) — ~12x too many notes lit at once; the original's waterfall shows one sparse descending chain of ~8 notes in 7 s, the port's shows 3-4 simultaneous parallel diagonals. (b) GRID BRIGHTNESS/COLOUR: the original's cell separators are a bright orange (105,53,31) against filled cells of (5,2,1) and empty cells of exactly (0,0,0); the port's separators are a dim near-grey (25,23,20) against filled cells of (13,9,5) and empty cells of (2,1,1) — the port's grid is ~4x dimmer and desaturated, and its 'off' state is never truly black. (c) LIT FRACTION: original 0.607 of the rig lit in this mode, port 0.962.

AUDIO REACTIVITY (--sensors synth vs --sensors off, identical seed/window, byte-compared per dump). Neither side's opening ~6 s depends on the feed at all: 0/120 frames differ on BOTH sides over 0-5.95 s at 20 fps, so the 2 Hz pulsing in the bar mode is an INTERNAL 120 BPM timer on both, not beat detection. Over 90 s at 20 fps the ORIGINAL first becomes audio-dependent at t=18.9 s (the sequencer/note mode) and stays divergent thereafter (236/300 sampled frames differ); the PORT first diverges at t=8.1 s (its orange bloom mode; 248/300 differ). At 10 fps the picture changes for the port only: the original still first reacts at t=19.5 s, but the port's first audio-dependent frame moves out to t=35.4 s and only 15/133 sampled frames differ over 40 s (its 10 fps meanBrightness series is correlated 1.000 with the unfed run over the first 30 s). The port's audio path is therefore frame-rate-sensitive in a way the original's is not.

OVERALL LEVELS (strip-256, 180 s at 10 fps): original meanBrightness avg 12.0, max 46, mean R/G/B 20.0/4.7/10.6; port meanBrightness avg 17.0, max 79, mean R/G/B 28.5/14.0/8.5. The port runs ~40% brighter overall and is markedly greener and less blue than the original across the cycle. On the 6 s default-grid baseline the port's meanG and meanB are exactly 0 on all 120 frames while the original already carries a small blue component (meanB max 20) from its triangle-gradient mode at t~3.3 s.

DETERMINISM/ROBUSTNESS: both sides are seed-independent (seed 1 vs seed 7 dumps byte-identical at t=0.65/1.15/3.35 s on both sides), and both degrade gracefully with dead sensors (30 s at 10 fps with --sensors off: orig mean 12 motion 11, port mean 14 motion 13 — neither goes black or errors). Neither side has a warm-up transient or a dying steady state: both are still cycling normally at t=180 s, brightnessTrend volatile on both, zeroMotionFrames low on both.
feedback: PRIMARY FIX — pixel addressing. The original is index-only: every mode is a function of the flat pixel index alone, verified byte-identical across strip-256, grid 16x16 and grid 32x8. The port instead drives everything off the x coordinate, so on the default 16x16 grid it paints whole vertical columns (its output is constant down every column, only 16 distinct values per frame) where the original paints contiguous runs of the flat index. Re-map the port to index/pixelCount rather than x. This alone changes what a viewer sees on the default rig from 'vertical stripes' to the original's horizontal band / diagonal texture and is worth more than every other item on this list.

SPEED — the opening VU bar is ~4x too slow. Original: 260 px/s, the bar fills all 256 px in ~0.98 s (1/2 of the strip per 0.5 s beat) and then restarts from the opposite end. Port: 66 px/s, ~3.9 s per fill (1/8 of the strip per beat). Multiply the port's per-beat bar increment by 4.

BEAT ENVELOPE — the original's per-beat decay is LINEAR down to a genuinely black frame (229, 203, 178, 153, 127, 102, 76, 51, 25, 0 at 20 fps), with a constant 229 peak every beat. The port decays exponentially to a floor of ~90 (36% of peak) and never blanks, and its peak sags across a bar (249 -> 223). Make the decay linear-to-zero with a fixed re-strike level.

SUPER-CYCLE LENGTH — the original's mode rotation repeats every 27.0 s and is fps-invariant (27.5 / 26.9 / 26.5 s at 10 / 20 / 40 fps). The port's is 36.9 s at 20 fps (1.37x too long) and additionally moves with frame rate (43.3 s at 10 fps). Drive the mode advance off elapsed time (or off beats with a rate that does not depend on the render rate) and shorten it to ~27 s.

MISSING MODES — the original's cycle contains three looks the port has no analogue for: (a) a 60-px internally-graded block that PING-PONGS the full length of the strip with a ~1.05 s round trip at near-full brightness; (b) a full-strip symmetric TRIANGLE gradient peaking exactly at the mid pixel (128 distinct values across the strip), red with a slight blue tail (hue ~340), re-struck on every beat; (c) a 48-px block parked at the centre with a shifting red hue. The port instead spends ~8 s (vs the original's ~2 s) on the bar mode and inserts a full-strip orange bloom that the original does not have.

FAN-MODE PALETTE AND CHARACTER — the original's long mid-cycle mode is a PERSISTENT textured field (peak brightness never drops below ~184, profile broken into 4-14 separate lit runs, fine dither) whose hue walks blue(187deg) -> purple -> magenta -> red -> orange -> yellow-green(138deg). The port renders it as a smooth single-run field that STROBES on the beat (253 -> 58 between strikes) and expands outward from the centre, with a hue walk in the wrong half of the wheel: yellow-green(84deg) -> green -> cyan -> blue(231deg). Both the segmentation/texture and the hue range need changing; do not keep the beat-strobe.

SEQUENCER MODE — the cell lattice is already exact (36 cells, ~7.1 px pitch, one-cell-wide notes, same saturated primaries); only three things need fixing there. (1) Note density: the original lights 0.22 bright notes per frame, the port 2.60 — cut simultaneous notes by ~12x so the mode reads as one sparse descending chain, not 3-4 parallel diagonals. (2) Grid contrast: the original's cell separators are bright orange (105,53,31) with filled cells at (5,2,1) and empty cells at exactly (0,0,0); the port's separators are dim grey (25,23,20) with filled cells at (13,9,5) and empty cells at (2,1,1). Brighten and warm the separators ~4x and let empty cells go fully black. (3) Lit fraction in this mode should be ~0.61, not ~0.96.

AUDIO PATH — both sides run the bar mode off an internal 120 BPM timer (byte-identical with --sensors off for the first 6 s on both), so that part is fine. But the original's audio dependence starts at the same point in its cycle at 10 fps and at 20 fps (t=19.5 s vs 18.9 s, the note mode), while the port's moves from t=8.1 s at 20 fps to t=35.4 s at 10 fps and is almost absent at 10 fps (15/133 sampled frames differ vs the unfed run). Whatever history buffer the port's audio path keeps is sized in render frames rather than seconds; convert it to a time window so reactivity is identical at 10 and 20 fps.
NO CONTROL-SURFACE WORK NEEDED: both sides genuinely expose zero settable controls, confirmed by --probe-controls on the fixed original. Nothing to add or remove.
